title: Northstar: a small customer's migration
disclosure: Synthetic interview — fictional company and speaker

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: How did your small Northstar deployment migrate?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: Our small deployment moved in six weeks because we used only standard connectors.

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: We had twelve users and did not maintain custom integrations. This was one migration, not a representative survey.

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: I cannot estimate how an enterprise deployment would compare.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: Can you describe the initial steps you took to plan the migration? Were there any particular challenges you anticipated?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: We began by mapping out all our existing workflows within Northstar, focusing on those that used the standard connectors. Since we avoided custom integrations, the planning was straightforward. Our main concern was ensuring data integrity during the transfer, but because our setup was relatively simple, we didn't foresee major obstacles.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: During the six-week migration period, did you encounter any unexpected issues or delays? If so, how did you address them?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: We did face a minor delay when one of the connectors didn’t behave exactly as documented, causing a temporary halt in data synchronization. We reached out to Northstar support, who provided a workaround involving a slight adjustment in the connector configuration. That resolved the issue quickly, and we were back on track within a couple of days.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: You mentioned not using custom integrations. Did you consider any during the migration, or did you find the standard connectors sufficient for your needs?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: We evaluated the possibility of custom connectors early on, but given our small team and straightforward processes, the standard connectors covered all our requirements. This decision definitely simplified the migration and reduced complexity.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: How did you manage user training and adaptation during the migration? Were there any notable feedback or resistance from the team?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: Because the interface and workflows remained largely the same, the training was minimal. We held a couple of short sessions to familiarize users with any new features and the migration timeline. Overall, the team adapted well, with only a few questions here and there. There wasn’t significant resistance, likely because the changes were incremental rather than drastic.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: Looking back, is there anything you would do differently if you were to repeat the migration?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: If I had to do it again, I would allocate a bit more time upfront for testing each connector in a staging environment. We did some testing, but a more thorough approach might have caught the connector hiccup earlier, potentially avoiding the brief delay.

turns.speaker: Moderator
turns.text: Did you observe any impact on your daily operations during the migration? How did you mitigate any disruptions?

turns.speaker: Fictional operator
turns.text: We scheduled the most critical migration steps during off-peak hours and weekends to minimize disruption. There was a slight slowdown in workflow automation during the final switchover, but it was brief and didn’t significantly affect productivity. Good communication with the team helped manage expectations.
